subject: Statue of Liberty
title: The Statue of Liberty Wasn't Built Green. It Took About 20 Years

scenes.text: The Statue of Liberty wasn't green when it was unveiled.
In 1886 she was shiny reddish-brown, like a new penny. Her skin is copper as thin as two pennies.
Salty sea air and rain went to work. Within about 20 years, she was turning blue-green.
In 1906, Congress set aside money to paint her. People protested it would be sacrilege.
Good thing. That green crust is a patina, and it shields the copper underneath from corroding.
The green isn't damage. It's her armor.

description:
When it was unveiled in 1886, the Statue of Liberty was a shiny reddish-brown, the colour of a new penny. Its copper skin is about as thick as two pennies.
Reactions with air, rain and sea spray built a blue-green patina over roughly two decades. In 1906 Congress set aside $62,000 to paint it, but protests stopped the plan, and the patina now protects the copper beneath.
Would you have voted to paint her?
first_comment: Bartholdi reportedly expected her to darken to red, not turn green. What colour would you want her to be?
